title: Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to development, staging, and production environments.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications. Its primary job is to help you test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing deploying postgresql-based applications teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

items.title: Development, staging, and production environments
items.text: Match the index method and operator class to real query predicates, then compare the plan and write/storage costs.

items.title: Schema migration during deployment
items.text: Prefer additive changes first, test against populated sample data, and preserve compatibility while old and new code overlap.

items.title: Health checks and connection validation

items.title: Deployment rollback considerations
items.text: Mark the transaction boundary explicitly and verify both the commit path and a rollback path in a disposable database.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications
content_blocks.code:
# Python/psycopg 3 — illustrative, not run by the browser playground
import os
import psycopg

with psycopg.connect(os.environ['DATABASE_URL']) as conn:
    with conn.cursor() as cur:
        cur.execute('SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE id = %s', (42,))
        rows = cur.fetchall()
        print(rows)
content_blocks.expected_output: Prints the rows returned for product id 42, or an empty list when no row matches.
content_blocks.safety_note: CodeLeaf does not execute this Python snippet. Never run arbitrary learner code inside FastAPI or a production web process.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Requires psycopg 3, a configured DATABASE_URL, an existing products table and a separately isolated Python runner. Values use bound parameters.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For a read-only SELECT or inspection command, no reset is needed. For DDL/DML, use a disposable database; capture the starting state, run the example, inspect the result, and ROLLBACK or drop the lab objects as appropriate. Do not use production data or credentials.

Treat the sample as inspectable code unless you run it yourself in an approved isolated environment. Python examples require a separate isolated runner.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Safety checkpoint: use least-privilege credentials, synthetic data, and a separate test database; verify results before applying a change to a real workload.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Development, staging, and production environments”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Development, staging, and production environments”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications, with an explanation of “Development, staging, and production environments”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Deploying PostgreSQL-Based Applications fits into the broader goal to test data integrity and migration behavior, plan deployment boundaries and document a production readiness review.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Development, staging, and production environments, Secrets and environment configuration, Schema migration during deployment.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
